title: One-click stub-to-prod pricing playbook
content:
Purpose: capture a compact, developer-centric playbook for converting an early experiment (one-click stub or local mock) into a paid production integration on Redwood Hosted API. This is intentionally tactical: microcopy, quickstart steps, pricing anchors tied to developer behaviors, and short objection-handling scripts.

Context and problem:
- Developers often try APIs with a tiny stub or local mock. They hit two friction points when moving toward real usage: (1) uncertainty about cost for real traffic patterns, (2) lack of a clear, low-effort path to upgrade from a throwaway token/stub to a production key with predictable billing.
- Our existing material talks about speed and docs but doesn't explicitly map stub->trial->commit paths or give cost heuristics tied to common dev flows (chat UI, embeddings search, batch inference).

Target personas:
- Indie dev / early startup engineer: wants simple onboarding, clear cost floor, and a way to demo to stakeholders.
- Product engineer at mid-market company: cares about predictable costs, security (no leaked tokens), and upgrade path to Dedicated.
- Platform/infra engineer evaluating for enterprise: wants telemetry, quotas, and migration story to Dedicated or Private.

Core promises (developer-first language):
- "From one click to production: try a real Redwood endpoint in minutes, keep the same SDK and routing when you scale."
- "No surprise billing: quick cost check tools estimate token spend for your sample prompts before you hit production."
- "Upgrade without rework: exchange the throwaway key for a production key, keep model pinning and rollout settings intact."

Quickstart flow (micro UX copy + steps):
1) "Run a local stub (1-click)": Copy a single command; start a temporary stub token that mimics responses.
   - microcopy: "Spin up a sample Redwood endpoint locally — no card required."
2) "Swap to a real key (one step)": Click "promote" in Console or run rwictl auth promote --token <stub>.
   - microcopy: "Promote this integration to a real API key. Keep your routes and model selection."
3) "Estimate cost (instant)": Console shows a quick estimate based on your sample payloads and projected qps.
   - microcopy: "Estimated monthly cost for current test traffic: $X–$Y (based on tokens and embedding units)."
4) "Choose billing path": Pay-as-you-go or reserved (Dedicated) recommendation based on projected peak qps.
   - microcopy: "Prefer predictable spend? Reserve capacity starting at 2M tokens/day and save ~20%"

Pricing anchors and heuristics (for microcopy and sales scripts):
- Anchor A — experimental: "Free trial credit + PAYG; prototypes typically cost < $10/week for low-volume chat demos (1k–10k tokens/day)."
- Anchor B — scale-to-demo: "A demo expected to handle 50 concurrent visitors (avg 200 tokens/session) will run ~2M tokens/month => PAYG cost estimate: $Z/month (show calculator)."
- Anchor C — low-latency webapp: "If you require 99th pctl latency <150ms and burst capacity, Dedicated starts to make sense at sustained 10M tokens/month."

Note: exact dollar values should be filled by pricing ops; playbook uses these as framing language for docs, not price-setting.

Pricing language templates (short snippets for UI and docs):
- For UI trial banner: "Start for free — upgrade in one click. No rework, exportable logs, and predictable cost estimates."
- For billing step: "Choose Pay-as-you-go to start; pick Reserved Capacity when you need predictable latency and price certainty."
- For pricing FAQ: "How much will integration cost? Use our cost estimator or run a sample suite (link) — prototypes are inexpensive; production costs scale with tokens and embedding units."

Competitive differentiation notes (how to position vs incumbents):
- Against generic cloud endpoints: emphasize "same SDK and routing across hosted, dedicated, private" and the one-click promotion path.
- Against LLM-API-first players: lean on production tooling (cost estimator, model pinning, rollout policies) and the stub->prod migration story.
- Against self-hosted runtimes: emphasize "start instantly, migrate later" and the developer velocity benefit.

Objection-handling scripts (short):
- "I’m worried about surprise bills": "We provide an instant estimator before upgrade and settable hard usage caps to protect you from accidental spend."
- "I don’t want to change code when we scale": "Production keys keep your same routes and SDKs; Dedicated is a capacity config and not a code change."
- "We need SSO and audit logs": "Private or Dedicated plan includes SSO and long-term audit logs — early access available via account rep."

Measurement and success signals (what to track after rollout):
- Conversion funnel: stub deploys -> promoted-to-real-key -> first paid charge -> month-two retention.
- Time-to-upgrade median (target < 48 hours for trial users who hit production signifiers).
- Estimator usage: % of promoted integrations that used the cost estimator before upgrade.
- Churn reasons capturing: (cost, latency, security) via short survey when downgrading.

Implementation notes for docs/console/SDKs (engineering asks):
- Console: add a prominent "Promote stub" CTA on trial integration card with inline cost estimate and hard cap toggle.
- SDK: add a helper method to detect stub token and autocue promotion path (e.g., Redwood.isStubToken()).
- Quickstart repo: add a folder 'stub-to-prod' with three recipes (chat demo, embeddings search, batch job) that include sample payloads for estimator.

Copy snippets for email and sales outreach (short):
- "Try a Redwood endpoint now — demo in minutes, estimate costs before you commit, and upgrade without rework."
- For enterprise outreach: "We can run a reserve-sizing consult based on your sample traffic and deliver a Dedicated proposal in 2–3 days."

Open questions / TODOs:
- Pricing ops: supply a set of public number bands (prototype / demo / production / enterprise) we can reference in estimator and microcopy.
- Legal/Security: confirm language we can use around "no card required" during stub trials and what token TTLs are acceptable for security guidance.
- Engineering: ETA for stub promote UX and SDK hook.

Next steps (owners & deadlines):
- Product marketing (Asha): finalize microcopy and email snippets by 2026-03-15.
- Pricing ops (Diego): publish banded pricing guidance draft by 2026-03-22.
- Console eng (Evelyn): prototype "promote stub" card by 2026-04-05.
- SDK (Samir): add Redwood.isStubToken() helper + docs example by 2026-04-12.

Appendix: sample one-click commands for quickstart README (to be copy-edited into README):
1) Start stub locally: curl https://playground.redwood.dev/stub/start -d '{"template":"chat-demo"}'
2) Test call: curl https://playground.redwood.dev/your-stub -H 'Authorization: Bearer STUB_XXX' -d '{"prompt":"Hello"}'
3) Promote: rwictl auth promote --stub STUB_XXX --team acme -> returns PRODUCTION_KEY_ABC

Notes: keep this doc intentionally operational — the goal is to give field teams and docs writers a small set of ready-to-use lines, example flows, and a prioritized engineering ask list so we can ship the one-click promotion experience quickly.
